title: Instruction Safety of the Generated Program
statement: For every natural number $E$, every finite Boolean word $x$, and every configuration of the generated register program, the instruction safety conditions hold: an active register-equality test compares distinct registers; a test comparing a register with the input payload occurs only when $x$ is a valid plain encoding; tests comparing a register with either inner payload occur only when $x$ is a valid paired encoding; and every decider call has a list of pairwise distinct argument registers. A halted configuration or a configuration whose active instruction is a nondeterministic choice satisfies the condition without further restrictions.
replaced:
For every natural number $E$, every input bit string $x$, and every configuration of the
register program specified by the control flow in the definitions above, the active
deterministic instruction satisfies the following safety conditions: an equality test
between registers compares distinct registers; an equality test between a register and
the input payload is used only when $x$ is a valid plain encoding; either equality test
against an inner payload is used only when $x$ is a valid paired encoding; and every
decider call uses pairwise distinct registers as arguments. Configurations with no
active label, and labels at which the program makes a nondeterministic choice, impose no
further condition.
